newsitem.title: UK: CAA faces pressure on BAA pricing says pape.
newsitem.headline: CAA faces pressure on BAA pricing says pape.

text.p: Delays in building a fifth passenger terminal at London Heathrow airport is likely to put pressure on Britain's Civil Aviation Authority to review the level of airline user fees it allows airport operator BAA Plc to charge, The Times newspaper said in a report on Monday.

The 1.5 billion pounds project has been held up by the hugely protracted process of a public planning inquiry into whether the project to increase passenger capacity at Heathrow to over 80 million passengers a year should be allowed to go ahead.

The newspaper said the prospect of a two to three-year delay to the terminal's scheduled opening date of 2002 was "creating alarm and confusion in the City and a drastic shift in BAA's expenditure plans might prompt demands for a (airline user pricing) review."
The CAA regulates the level of airline charges at BAA's London Heathrow, Gatwick and Stansted airports.
But in its last five-yearly review, completed last October, the CAA ruled that BAA should change its prices by three percentage points below inflation each year for the next five years to April 2002.
It said it deliberately set a relatively benign formula to encourage BAA to go ahead with Terminal Five and to help spread out the impact of the project on future pricing reviews.
"The CAA chose to smooth the pricing formula allowing BAA a relatively high return over the five years from 1997," said the report in The Times.
"Pushing Terminal Five to 2005 makes the formula look even more lenient," the paper said, adding that there were some fears that Terminal Five could end up being almost five years late.

The regulated charges accounted for 28 percent of BAA's total revenues of around 1.25 billion pounds in the year to March 31 1995. Retail income totalled 556 million pounds, making airport shopping BAA's biggest single earner.
